description: IS_VECTOR - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. It is TRUE for both element types, and FALSE for everything else VARIANT can hold: a plain ARRAY, an OBJECT, a PARSE_JSON array, a NUMBER and a BOOLEAN - an array that merely LOOKS like a vector is not one. The trap that makes this function unlike the rest of the IS_* family is NULL: IS_VECTOR(NULL) and IS_VECTOR(NULL::VECTOR(FLOAT,3)) are both SQL NULL rather than FALSE. A non-VARIANT argument is a compile error naming its type, and the vector type is tracked through a stored column, a derived table and a CTE. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/IsVectorTest (now retired); the Java's assertRejected only asserted that something threw, so the converted tests pin the exact live messages instead.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE isvec_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT IS_VECTOR(v) FROM isvec_rows WHERE id = 1
SELECT IS_VECTOR(v) FROM isvec_rows WHERE id = 2
WITH t AS (SELECT [1,2,3]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3) AS v) SELECT IS_VECTOR(v) FROM t
